tone_statements.citation: Myar Doo Myar Reh. 2004. A phonological comparison of selected Karenic language varieties of Kayah State. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xix+180 pp. (Monumanaw = Monu dialect of Dolaso, Phruso township).
tone_statements.quote: According to this data, there are four contrastive tones in Monumanaw. Each tone is referred to by demonstrating diacritics. They are high //, high-mid //, mid // and low //. … There are four contranstive tones in Monumanaw. With three syllable words this means that there are sixty-four possible patterns. … four phoneme tones occur in Kayah, Kayaw and Monumanaw. No falling and rising tones occur in Kayah, Kayaw and Monumanaw.

Sec. 3.3 Monumanaw (pp. 90-109): syllable types CVT and CCVT, 22 consonants, 14 clusters, 10 vowels, four contrastive tones (high, high-mid, mid, low); p. 108: in three-syllable words 'There are no examples of M or HM occurring on the first or second syllable.. strong tendency for them to also not occur on the final syllable' (tone distribution, not a stress statement). Ch. 4 p. 136: template C1(C2)V T, open syllables only.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.8 'Brief Phonology of Kayah Monu' (pp. 11-14, pp. 27-30) gives 22 consonants, 10 vowels, four contrastive tones (footnote: researcher hypothesises only three level tones), open syllables only, 'template for main syllable structure is C1(C2)V'; phonology explicitly taken from Myar 2004. a full-text search for stress/accent/unstressed/sesquisyllabic/minor syllable/iambic/prominence: no hits (only dialect 'accent'). Affixation section (2.4.2, prefixes ta-, ʔə-) says nothing prosodic.

sources.note: Sec. IV.2 'Transcription' states that the source's tone letters are reclassified as diacritics and that Kayah Monu (like Brek Kayaw) has the 'typical four-way opposition' high / high-mid / mid / low, all level; Yintale additionally has rising and falling contours and breathiness. Secondhand restatement of Myar 2004's four-tone analysis; every Monu form in the 110-item list carries a tone mark. Nothing on stress.
